title: Set up your workshop
why: Every later module assumes these tools work. One evening of proper setup saves weeks of friction, and the habits you set here (secrets out of Git, a commit every session) carry through the whole route.
outcomes: Python, uv, VS Code and Git working on your machine
A public GitHub repo with a README that states your goal
An LLM API key stored safely, with a spend limit
A local model running through Ollama, so you can practise for free
Your 15 weekly hours blocked in your calendar
lessons: Install Python 3.12 or newer and uv, then create a project with uv init
Install VS Code with the Python, Pylance and Ruff extensions (on Windows, set up WSL2 first)
Install Git, create a GitHub account and push your first repo
Open an Anthropic or OpenAI API account, set a £10 spend limit, keep the key in a .env file that .gitignore excludes
Install Ollama and run a small local model from the terminal
Block the weekly rhythm in your calendar (Toolkit, Weekly rhythm)
resources: The project and package manager used throughout
method: Set up once and set up properly. Keep a SETUP.md as you go: the next time a tool breaks, your own notes will be faster than any forum.
build: A public repo called ai-engineering-log with a README stating your goal, your weekly rhythm and the date you started.

quiz.q: What is the best guard against tutorial hell?
o: Finishing every course before building anything
Ending each session by committing something you built
quiz.e: A commit per session forces output. Courses feel productive; shipped code is what counts and what employers see.

quiz.q: Why give each project its own virtual environment?
o: It isolates each project's dependencies so versions don't clash
quiz.e: Isolated environments stop one project's package versions breaking another's, and make builds reproducible.

quiz.q: Where should an API key live in your project?
o: Hard-coded at the top of main.py
In the README so others can run it
In a .env file excluded by .gitignore, or a secrets store
quiz.e: Keys in Git history get scraped within minutes. Use environment variables locally and the platform's secret store when deployed.

o: Uploads your local commits to the remote repository
quiz.e: Commit saves locally; push sends those commits to GitHub.

quiz.q: Why run a local model with Ollama while learning?
o: You can practise prompting and pipelines without spending on API calls
It is needed to use Python
quiz.e: Ollama lets you build and iterate for free, then switch to a hosted model when quality matters.
